home.hero_title: Zoozen, the platform that will give you precise details about the animal world.
home.hero_textOne: Welcome to the world of Zoozen, your new digital haven dedicated to the beauty and diversity of the animal kingdom. Whether you're a wildlife conservationist, a furry friend, or simply curious to uncover nature's secrets, you've come to the right place. Explore our detailed profiles, discover fascinating species, and join a community that beats to the rhythm of the planet's heartbeat. Together, let's celebrate wildlife in all its forms!
home.hero_textTwo: Explore the animal kingdom like never before with Zoozen. Our platform brings together precise classifications and essential information on the species that inhabit our planet, from the ocean depths to the highest peaks. Designed for enthusiasts and curious minds, Zoozen simplifies access to animal knowledge through an intuitive interface and richly documented content. Dive into discovery and be amazed by the world's wildlife.
home.hero_textThree: Welcome to Zoozen, the ultimate destination for all animal lovers. From the tiniest creatures to the majestically grand, we'll take you on a journey to meet those who share our planet. Ready for a total immersion in the heart of the living world? Start your exploration now!
home.animal_title: Are you interested in this animal ?
home.videoTextOne: Because every species matters, Zoozen opens the doors to a world where nature reclaims its rights. Our mission is to reconnect humans with the wild by highlighting the fragility and splendor of biodiversity. From coral reefs to the savannah plains, embark on an educational and engaging journey. Learning about them is the first step towards protecting them.
home.videoTextTwo: Did you know that some animals possess incredible abilities that surpass fiction? Welcome to Zoozen, the playground for all budding explorers! Here, we dissect animal lifestyles, compare their records, and marvel at nature's most unusual facts. Pack your virtual backpack, the wild adventure begins here!
home.videoTextThree: Welcome to Zoozen, the meeting place for humans and their best friends. Whether you share your life with a four-legged companion or dream of faraway encounters, we offer you the keys to better understand their language, their needs, and their world. A daily source of inspiration for all those who consider animals to be full-fledged members of the family.
home.factMysteryOne: The lion's roar can be heard up to 8 kilometers away. It allows lions to mark their territory and signal their position to members of the pride without having to travel long distances.
home.factMysteryTwo: Butterflies have taste receptors on their legs. This allows them to check if a leaf is edible or suitable for laying eggs simply by landing on it.
home.factMysteryThree: Bees can recognize human faces. They do not look at each detail in isolation (a nose, an eye), but they memorize the relative arrangement of the facial features.
home.factMysteryFour: Crows are capable of recognizing human faces and remembering those that have been hostile towards them, even passing this information on to their peers.
home.factMysteryFive: To avoid drowning, dolphins only sleep one cerebral hemisphere at a time. One eye remains open to watch for predators while the other half of the brain rests.
home.factMysterySix: A housefly processes images about seven times faster than a human. To it, our movements appear to be in slow motion, which explains why it is so difficult to catch.
home.factMysterySeven: Turritopsis dohrnii is capable of reversing its life cycle. When stressed or sick, it reverts to its polyp (baby) stage, theoretically allowing it to live indefinitely.
home.factMysteryHeight: Koalas have fingerprints that are almost identical to those of humans, to the point that they have sometimes confused investigators at crime scenes.
home.factMysteryNine: The pistol shrimp snaps its claw so hard that it creates a cavitation bubble reaching temperatures close to that of the sun's surface, stunning its prey with the shock wave.
home.factMysteryTen: Some species of ants practice aphid farming, protecting them from predators in order to harvest in return the sweet honeydew they produce.
home.factMysteryEleven: Her heart is so large that a human being could swim through its arteries. However, it only beats 2 to 10 times per minute when she dives.
home.factMysteryTwelve: A giraffe's heart weighs approximately 11 kilograms to pump blood to its brain. Its heart has extremely thick muscular walls (up to 7 cm) to generate this force.
